blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content: This paper devotes to Gröbner-Shirshov bases for small categories (all categories below are supposed to be small) presented by a graph (=quiver) and defining relations (see, Maclane [@Sa; @M]). As important examples, we use the simpicial and the cyclic categories (see, for example, Maclane [@Sa], Gelfand, Manin [@G]). In an above presentation, a category is viewed as a "monoid with several objects\". blocks.title: A short survey on Gröbner-Shirshov bases
blocks.content:
What is now called Gröbner and Gröbner-Shirshov bases theory was initiated by A. I. Shirshov (1921-1981) [@Sh62a; @Sh62b], 1962 for non-associative and Lie algebras, by H. Hironaka [@Hi64; @{Hi64-}], 1964 for quotients of commutative infinite series algebras (both formal and convergent), and by B. Buchberger [@bu65; @bu70], 1965, 1970 for commutative algebras.

English translation of selected works of A. I. Shirshov, including [@Sh62a; @Sh62b], is recently published [@Shir3].

Note that for $f,g\in kC(X)$ if we write $gf$, it means $gf$ is defined.
